title: LEvOsimendaN vs. Placebo Before Tricuspid VAlve Surgery in Patients with Right Ventricular Dysfunction
official: LEONARD. Levosimendan vs. Placebo Before Isolated Tricuspid Valve Surgery
summary: Main objective: To assess the efficacy of preoperative levosimendan in preventing postoperative death and low cardiac output in patients undergoing isolated tricuspid valve surgery for severe tricuspid regurgitation.
conditions: Patients referred for an isolated tricuspid valve surgery for  severe tricuspid regurgitation

interventions.name: ZIMINO 2,5 mg/ml, solution à diluer pour perfusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years
2. Written signed informed consent
3. Affiliation to the French health care system (Sécurité Sociale)
4. Patients referred for correction of an isolated tricuspid valve surgery for severe tricuspid regurgitation (effective regurgitant orifice (ERO) ≥40mm² or vena contracta ≥7mm or integrative approach)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Severe hypotension defined by systolic blood pressure <90mmHg
2. History of torsade de pointe
3. Organic renal failure defined by creatinine clearance <30mL/min
4. Recent endocarditis (<3 months)
5. Recent myocardial infarction (<3 months)
6. Congenital TR
7. Cardiogenic shock requiring dobutamine support or cardiac assistance
8. Severe liver injury (CHILD C)
9. Left-sided valvular heart disease > grade 2
10. Concomitant intervention (aortic valve, mitral valve, aorta, CABG)
11. Heart transplant patient
12. Left ventricular obstruction
13. Allergy to levosimedan
14. Current participation in other investigational drug or device studies or being in the exclusion period at the end of a previous study involving human participants, if applicable
15. Pregnant or breastfeeding women
16. Females of childbearing potential without effective method of birth control
17. Patient on AME (state medical aid) unless exemption from affiliation
18. Patient under guardianship (under “tutelle or curatelle or sauvegarde de justice or mandat de protection futur activé ou habilitation familiale” according to French law
19. Severe tachycardia (>150/bpm)
